quizzes.title: CJI Appointment and Collegium Rulings
quizzes.passage: The appointment of judges to the Supreme Court has been a subject of repeated litigation in India, and the Court has ruled on it several times. For a long period after the Court was set up, the seniormost judge of the Supreme Court was generally appointed Chief Justice of India. This practice was set aside twice in the 1970s, when the government chose judges who were not the seniormost. The Constitution requires the President to consult certain persons before appointing judges, and the meaning of the word consultation became a dispute. The First Judges Case of 1981 examined this word. The Second Judges Case of 1993 later revisited the question of how the Chief Justice of India should be chosen. The Third Judges Case of 1998 dealt with the process that the Chief Justice must follow before sending recommendations to the Government. Parliament later sought to replace the collegium with a new body, the National Judicial Appointments Commission, through a constitutional amendment and an Act. The Fourth Judges Case of 2015 examined that amendment and the Act. The rulings are known as the First, Second, Third and Fourth Judges Cases. The 1973 and 1977 appointments were made by the government of the time.

questions.q: In the Third Judges Case (1998), how many judges giving an adverse opinion would stop the CJI from sending a recommendation to the Government?
questions.explanation: The Third Judges Case held that if two judges give an adverse opinion, no recommendation is sent to the Government.

questions.q: In which year were the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act and the National Judicial Appointments Commission Act enacted?
questions.explanation: Both the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act and the NJAC Act were enacted in 2014.

questions.q: Which judgment held that the advice tendered by the Chief Justice of India is binding on the President in matters of appointment of judges?
questions.explanation: The Second Judges Case (1993) ruled that the CJI's advice on appointments is binding on the President.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Under the Second Judges Case (1993), only the seniormost judge of the Supreme Court should be appointed Chief Justice of India.
Reason (R): The National Judicial Appointments Commission Act was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2015.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A is true as stated in the 1993 ruling, but R is false because the Court declared the NJAC Act void in 2015.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Chairperson of the NJAC   ->   A. Chief Justice of India
II. Eminent persons to be nominated to the NJAC   ->   B. Nominated by CJI, PM and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
III. Union Law Minister   ->   C. Ex-officio member of the NJAC
IV. Fourth Judges Case (2015)   ->   D. Declared the NJAC and 99th Amendment void
questions.explanation: The CJI chairs the NJAC, eminent persons are nominated by CJI, PM and Leader of Opposition, the Law Minister is ex-officio, and the 2015 case voided the NJAC.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The First Judges Case (1981) held that consultation only implies exchange of views.
II. The Third Judges Case (1998) held that the sole opinion of the Chief Justice of India constitutes consultation.
III. The Fourth Judges Case (2015) declared the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act and the NJAC Act void.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the Third Judges Case required consultation with a collegium of senior judges, not the CJI's sole opinion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The First Judges Case (1981) held that consultation means concurrence.
II. One of the two eminent persons to be nominated to the NJAC must be from SC/ST/OBC/Minorities or Women.
III. If one judge gives an adverse opinion, the CJI must not send a recommendation to the Government.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement II is correct, since the 1981 case held that consultation only implies exchange of views and two adverse opinions, not one, stop a recommendation.

quizzes.title: CJI Appointment and Collegium Recall
quizzes.passage: Judicial appointments in India have been shaped by a series of decisions over several decades. The Constitution provides that judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President, and that the Chief Justice of India is appointed after consultation with judges the President considers necessary. For a long period after the Court was set up, the most senior judge was usually chosen to lead the Court as its head. That pattern was broken twice in the 1970s. Later, the Supreme Court interpreted the word consultation in the context of appointments. The Third Judges Case addressed the steps the Chief Justice must take before advising the government. The Second Judges Case addressed the advice tendered by the Chief Justice and the judges he consults. A proposal to create a National Judicial Appointments Commission was made through a constitutional amendment and an Act of Parliament. The Court examined that amendment and Act in 2015. The cases raised questions about the weight to be given to the Chief Justice's view and about the place of the government in appointments. The rulings are commonly known by their ordinal numbers, such as the First and Second Judges Cases. Each judgment discussed here is known by its year and by the question it addressed.

questions.q: Which numbered Constitutional Amendment created the National Judicial Appointments Commission? (give the number only)
questions.explanation: The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act was the amendment that set up the NJAC, and the Court later struck it down.

questions.q: How many seniormost Supreme Court judges are ex-officio members of the NJAC? (number)
questions.explanation: The NJAC included two seniormost Supreme Court judges as ex-officio members.

questions.q: When AN Ray was appointed Chief Justice of India in 1973, how many senior judges were superseded? (number)
questions.explanation: AN Ray was appointed by superseding three senior judges: JM Shelat, KS Hegde and AN Grover.

questions.q: Under the Second Judges Case, after consulting how many of his seniormost colleagues does the CJI tender advice? (number)
questions.explanation: The Second Judges Case required the CJI to tender advice after consulting two of his seniormost colleagues.

questions.q: According to the Fourth Judges Case, the NJAC would affect which principle of the judiciary? (two words)
questions.explanation: The Court opined that the NJAC would affect the independence of the judiciary.

questions.q: Which Union minister is an ex-officio member of the NJAC? (give the designation)
accept: Union Minister of Law and Justice
questions.explanation: The Union Minister of Law and Justice sits as an ex-officio member of the NJAC.

questions.q: In the Second Judges Case, the CJI's advice on appointments was held to be what for the President? (one word)
questions.explanation: The Court ruled that the advice tendered by the CJI on appointments is binding on the President.

quizzes.title: Jurisdiction and Temporary Benches
quizzes.passage: The Supreme Court of India exercises more than one kind of jurisdiction. It hears appeals against decisions of lower courts, decides certain disputes at the first instance, and gives advice when asked. A person whose Fundamental Rights have been violated may approach the Court directly, which gives the Court a role beyond routine appeals. The President of India can also refer questions of public importance to the Court. The Constitution provides for situations in which the Court may need a temporary head or additional judges. One provision deals with the office of the Chief Justice of India when that office is vacant or cannot be filled, while others allow the Chief Justice to draw on judges who are not part of the regular bench. Such provisions are meant for specific circumstances and carry their own conditions. Some of these arrangements involve a retired judge or a High Court judge. The Court's jurisdiction is therefore divided into several parts, each set out in the Constitution. The arrangements described above allow the Court to continue its work when its regular composition is incomplete or its head is unavailable. Each of these provisions is a separate route, and a reader must know which one applies to a given situation.

questions.q: Under which Article can a person approach the Supreme Court directly for the violation of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 allows a direct approach to the Supreme Court for violation of Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: The advisory opinion that the Supreme Court gives when the President seeks it under Article 143 is what for the President?
questions.explanation: The advisory opinion of the Supreme Court under Article 143 is not binding on the President of India.

questions.q: Under Article 126, from which category is an Acting Chief Justice of India appointed?
options: Chief Justice of a High Court
questions.explanation: The President can appoint a Judge of the Supreme Court as Acting CJI when the CJI's office is vacant or the CJI cannot perform duties.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The President of India can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court under Article 143 on a question of public importance.
Reason (R): The opinion of the Supreme Court given under this power is not binding on the President.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but R describes the binding status of the opinion and does not explain why the President can seek it.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 126   ->   A. Acting Chief Justice of India
II. Article 127   ->   B. Ad hoc judge for lack of quorum
III. Article 128   ->   C. Retired judge sitting temporarily
IV. Article 131   ->   D. Disputes between Government of India and States
questions.explanation: Article 126 covers an Acting CJI, Article 127 ad hoc judges, Article 128 retired judges and Article 131 original disputes between the Union and States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 134A requires a High Court certificate for an appeal that involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution.
II. Under Article 128, a retired judge may sit only with the previous consent of the President and of the person to be appointed.
III. Under Article 127, the CJI can appoint an ad hoc judge without the previous consent of the President.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because Article 127 requires the President's previous consent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Government of India and one or more States.
II. The CJI can appoint an Acting Chief Justice of India under Article 126.
III. Article 32 allows a direct approach to the Supreme Court for violation of Fundamental Rights.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the President, not the CJI, appoints an Acting CJI.

quizzes.title: Jurisdiction and Temporary Benches Recall
quizzes.passage: The Supreme Court of India has a few separate routes into its work. Ordinary cases arrive as appeals from lower courts. Some disputes can be filed straight in the Supreme Court because of their nature, such as disputes between the Union and the States. Individuals can also approach the Court directly when their rights are violated. The head of the state may seek the Court's advice on questions of public importance. When the office of the Chief Justice is empty or the Chief Justice cannot act, another judge may take charge. When the Court lacks enough judges to hold a sitting, a High Court judge may be called in temporarily. A retired judge may also be asked to sit for a temporary period. Each of these situations is governed by a specific provision of the Constitution, and the provision must be read with its conditions. The Court's appellate, original and advisory roles together define the scope of its work, and the provisions for temporary arrangements support those roles. Some of these provisions apply to the Chief Justice, while others apply to judges who are not part of the regular bench, and the booklet describes each of them. Each is described with its own conditions.

questions.q: Under which Article can the CJI appoint a High Court judge as an ad hoc judge of the Supreme Court? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 127 allows the CJI to appoint an ad hoc judge when there is a lack of quorum of permanent judges.

questions.q: Under which Article can a retired Supreme Court or High Court judge be requested to sit as a Supreme Court judge for a temporary period? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 128 allows the CJI to request a retired judge to sit temporarily, with the consent of the President and the person.

questions.q: Under which Article can the President appoint an Acting Chief Justice of India? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 126 covers an Acting CJI when the CJI's office is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform duties.

questions.q: Under which Article does the Supreme Court have original jurisdiction over disputes between the Government of India and one or more States? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Union and the States.

questions.q: Under which Article must a High Court certify that a case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, before an appeal can be made to the Supreme Court? (include the suffix)
questions.explanation: Article 134A requires the High Court's certificate for such appeals.

questions.q: Under Article 127, before the CJI appoints a High Court judge as ad hoc judge, consultation is needed with which Chief Justice? (give the office)
questions.answer: Chief Justice of the High Court
accept: Chief Justice of the High Court concerned
Chief Justice of that High Court
questions.explanation: Under Article 127 the CJI must consult the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned before appointing an ad hoc judge.

questions.q: Under which Article can a person approach the Supreme Court directly when Fundamental Rights are violated? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 32 allows a direct approach to the Supreme Court for violation of Fundamental Rights.
